observation_summary: The date parser fails to correctly handle February 29th when parsing month and day fields, throwing an IllegalFieldValueException because it incorrectly validates the day against a non-leap year range (1-28) instead of the leap year range (1-29).
reasoning_summary: The issue is that the parsing logic (specifically in DateTimeParserBucket) does not correctly account for the year when validating the day-of-month field. The parser attempts to set the day before the year has been correctly determined or applied in the context of the leap year calculation. This is a procedural error in the parsing algorithm where the order of operations or the state used for validation is incorrect, leading to an invalid range check.
evidence_used: org.joda.time.IllegalFieldValueException: Cannot parse "2 29": Value 29 for dayOfMonth must be in the range [1,28]

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the error manifests as a failed check in verifyValueBounds, the root cause is the algorithmic failure to correctly determine the year context before performing the validation, rather than a missing or incorrect guard condition itself.
This is a procedural logic error in how the parser handles field updates, not a missing capability or design-level omission.
